bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷七 唐本紀第七: 愍帝 廢帝
title.en: Volume 7 Later Tang Annals 4: Deposed Emperors
title.raw: 卷七 唐本紀第七: 愍帝 廢帝 Volume 7 Later Tang Annals 4: Deposed Emperors

sentences.zh: 愍皇帝，明宗第五子從厚也。

translations.literal: Emperor Min was Mingzong’s fifth son, Conghou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min was Conghou, the fifth son of Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 為人形質豐厚，寡言好禮，明宗以其貌類己，特愛之。

translations.literal: As a man he was broad and substantial in build, sparing of speech, and fond of ritual; Mingzong especially loved him because his appearance resembled his own.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad and solid in build, quiet, and fond of ritual. Mingzong loved him especially because he looked like him.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，以檢校司徒拜河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，加檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, as acting Minister over the Masses he was appointed governor of Henan and supervisor of the Six Armies and the various Guards, and was additionally made acting Grand Guardian and joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng 2, with the title acting Minister over the Masses, he was appointed governor of Henan and supervisor of the Six Armies and the Guards; he was also given the titles acting Grand Guardian and joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 從厚妃，孔循女也，安重誨怒循以女妻從厚，三年，罷循樞密使，出從厚為宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Conghou’s consort was the daughter of Kong Xun; An Chonghui was angry that Xun had married his daughter to Conghou, and in the third year dismissed Xun as privy commissioner and sent Conghou out as military governor of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Conghou’s consort was Kong Xun’s daughter. An Chonghui was angered that Kong Xun had married her to Conghou; in the third year, Xun was removed as privy commissioner and Conghou was sent out as military governor of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙鎮河東。

translations.literal: The next year, he was transferred to guard Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, he was transferred to the Hedong command.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，封從厚宋王，徙鎮成德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing, Conghou was enfeoffed as Prince of Song and transferred to guard Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 1, Conghou was made Prince of Song and transferred to the Chengde command.

sentences.zh: 二年，徙鎮天雄，累加兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to guard Tianxiong and was repeatedly promoted up to concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was transferred to Tianxiong and eventually given the additional title concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，秦王從榮伏誅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, Congrong, Prince of Qin, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, Congrong, Prince of Qin, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 明宗病甚，遣宦者孟漢瓊召王于鄴，而明宗崩，祕其喪六日。

translations.literal: Mingzong was gravely ill and sent the eunuch Meng Hanqiong to summon the prince from Ye, but Mingzong died, and his death was kept secret for six days.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong became gravely ill, he sent the eunuch Meng Hanqiong to summon the prince from Ye. Mingzong then died, and his death was kept secret for six days.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸卯朔，發喪于西宮，皇帝即位于柩前，羣臣見於東階，復于喪位。

translations.literal: On the guimao new moon of the twelfth month, the mourning was announced in the Western Palace; the emperor took the throne before the coffin, the assembled ministers appeared at the eastern steps, and then returned to their mourning places.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao new moon of the twelfth month, the death was announced in the Western Palace. The emperor ascended before the coffin; the assembled ministers presented themselves at the eastern steps and then returned to their mourning positions.

sentences.zh: 丙午，成服于西宮。

translations.literal: On bingwu, mourning dress was completed in the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the court formally assumed mourning dress in the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 二代五君，於此始見嗣君即位服喪之事，先君得其終，嗣君得其始，而免禍亂於臣民，於篡亂之世，稀見之事也，故特詳言之。

translations.literal: In two dynasties and five rulers, only here is there first seen the matter of a successor ruler taking the throne and wearing mourning, with the former ruler obtaining his end and the successor ruler obtaining his beginning, and disaster and disorder being avoided among ministers and people; in an age of usurpation and disorder, this was a rarely seen affair, and therefore it is spoken of in special detail.
translations.idiomatic: Across two dynasties and five rulers, this is the first case in which a successor took the throne and observed mourning: the former ruler had a proper end, the successor a proper beginning, and ministers and people were spared disaster. In an age of usurpation and disorder, this was rare, so the text records it in special detail.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，登光政門樓，存問軍民。

translations.literal: On gengxu, he ascended the Guangzheng gate tower and inquired after the soldiers and people.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, he mounted the Guangzheng Gate tower and addressed the soldiers and people.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，殺司衣王氏。

translations.literal: On xinhai, he killed the Wardrobe Attendant Lady Wang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, he killed Lady Wang, the Wardrobe Attendant.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，始聽政。

translations.literal: On guichou, he first heard government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, he first attended to government business.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，殺司儀康氏。

translations.literal: On yimao, he killed the Ceremonial Attendant Lady Kang.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, he killed Lady Kang, the Ceremonial Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，馮道為大行皇帝山陵使，戶部尚書韓彥惲為副，中書舍人王延為判官，禮部尚書王權為禮儀使，兵部尚書李鏻為鹵簿使，御史中丞龍敏為儀仗使，左僕射權判河南府盧質為橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Feng Dao was made commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum, Minister of Revenue Han Yanyun was deputy, Secretariat Drafter Wang Yan was administrative judge, Minister of Rites Wang Quan was rites commissioner, Minister of War Li Lin was procession commissioner, Censor-in-chief Long Min was honor-guard commissioner, and Left Vice Director Lu Zhi, acting administrator of Henan prefecture, was commissioner for bridges, roads, stops, and relays.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Feng Dao was appointed commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum, with Minister of Revenue Han Yanyun as deputy. Wang Yan served as administrative judge, Wang Quan oversaw the rites, Li Lin the procession, Long Min the honor guard, and Lu Zhi the bridges, roads, lodging, and relays.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，禫。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the dan sacrifice was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the concluding mourning sacrifice was performed.

sentences.zh: 應順元年春正月壬申朔，視朝於廣壽殿。

translations.literal: In Yingshun 1, spring, on renshen the first day of the first month, he held court at Guangshou Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yingshun, on the new moon of the first month of spring, the Min Emperor held audience in Guangshou Hall.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，契丹使都督沒辣於來。

translations.literal: On yihai the Khitan envoy, commissioner Molayu, came.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai a Khitan envoy, the commissioner Molayu, arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，大赦，改元，用樂。

translations.literal: On wuyin a great amnesty was proclaimed, the reign title was changed, and music was used.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the throne proclaimed a general amnesty, altered the reign title, and restored court music.

sentences.zh: 回鶻可汗王仁美遣使者來。

translations.literal: The Uyghur khan Wang Renmei sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renmei, khan of the Uyghurs, dispatched envoys.

sentences.zh: 沙州、瓜州遣使者來。

translations.literal: Shazhou and Guazhou sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys came from Shazhou and Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，朱弘昭、馮赟獻錢助作山陵。

translations.literal: On yiwei Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun presented money to assist in building the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun offered funds toward Mingzong’s mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 閏月丙午，冊皇太后。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on bingwu, the empress dowager was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu of the intercalary month the empress dowager received her patent of investiture.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，冊太妃王氏。

translations.literal: On jiayin the consort dowager, Lady Wang, was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the consort dowager Lady Wang was formally invested.

sentences.zh: 北京留守石敬瑭獻銀絹助作山陵。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang, military governor and defender of the Northern Capital, presented silver and silk to assist in building the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang, who held Taiyuan as military governor and metropolitan defender, sent silver and silk for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 二月庚寅，視作山陵。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengyin, he inspected work on the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin of the second month he went in person to oversee the tomb works.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使潞王從珂反。

translations.literal: Congke, Prince of Lu and military governor of Fengxiang, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congke, Prince of Lu and military governor of Fengxiang, rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，西京留守王思同為西面行營都部署，靜難軍節度使藥彥稠為副。

translations.literal: On xinmao Wang Sitong, defender of the Western Capital, was made commander-in-chief of the western campaign army; Yao Yanchou, military governor of the Jingnan army, was made deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Wang Sitong, defender of Luoyang, was named commander-in-chief of the western field army, with Yao Yanchou of Jingnan as his second.

sentences.zh: 三月丙辰，思同兵潰，嚴衛指揮使尹暉、羽林指揮使楊思權以其軍叛降於從珂。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingchen, Sitong’s army was routed. Yin Hui, commander of the Yanwei guard, and Yang Siquan, commander of the Yulin guard, led their troops in defection and surrendered to Congke.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen of the third month Sitong’s force collapsed. Yin Hui of the Yanwei command and Yang Siquan of the Yulin command took their units over to Congke.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，殺侍衛親軍都指揮使朱弘實。

translations.literal: On xinyou Zhu Hongshi, commander-in-chief of the Palace Attendant Personal Army, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the court put to death Zhu Hongshi, commander of the Palace Attendant Personal Army.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，河陽三城節度使康義誠為鳳翔行營都招討使，王思同為副。

translations.literal: On guihai Kang Yicheng, military governor of the Heyang three cities, was made grand suppression commissioner of the Fengxiang campaign army; Wang Sitong was made deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Kang Yicheng of Heyang became grand suppression commissioner for the Fengxiang campaign, with Wang Sitong again as deputy.

sentences.zh: 西京副留守劉遂雍叛降於從珂，思同奔歸於京師，不克，死之。

translations.literal: Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of the Western Capital, rebelled and surrendered to Congke. Sitong fled back to the capital, could not prevail, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of Luoyang, went over to Congke. Sitong raced for the capital, failed to break through, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，京城巡檢使安從進叛，殺馮赟，朱弘昭自殺，從進傳其二首於從珂。

translations.literal: On dingmao An Congjin, capital city inspector, rebelled, killed Feng Yun, and Zhu Hongzhao killed himself. Congjin sent their two heads to Congke.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the capital inspector An Congjin mutinied, slew Feng Yun, and Zhu Hongzhao took his own life. Congjin forwarded both heads to Congke.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，如衛州。

translations.literal: On wuchen he went to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the Min Emperor withdrew to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 不書帝崩者，當於廢帝紀書弒鄂王也。

translations.literal: That it does not write that the emperor died is because it should write in Feidi’s annals that the Prince of E was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: The text does not say here that the emperor died because the event belongs in Feidi’s annals as the murder of the Prince of E.

sentences.zh: 廢帝，鎮州平山人也，本姓王氏，其世微賤，母魏氏，少寡，明宗為騎將，過平山，掠得之。

translations.literal: Feidi was a man of Pingshan in Zhenzhou; his original surname was Wang, his family was humble and lowly, and his mother, Lady Wei, was widowed young; when Mingzong was a cavalry officer and passed through Pingshan, he seized her.
translations.idiomatic: Feidi came from Pingshan in Zhenzhou. His original surname was Wang, and his family was humble. His mother, Lady Wei, was widowed young; Mingzong seized her when he passed through Pingshan as a cavalry officer.

sentences.zh: 魏氏有子阿三，已十餘歲，明宗養以為子，名曰從珂。

translations.literal: The Lady Wei had a son, Asan, already more than ten years old. Mingzong raised him as a son and named him Congke.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei already had a boy called Asan, past ten. Mingzong adopted him and gave him the name Congke.

sentences.zh: 及長，狀貌雄偉，謹信寡言，而驍勇善戰，明宗甚愛之。

translations.literal: When he grew up his bearing was imposing; he was cautious, trustworthy, and sparing of speech, yet fierce and skilled in battle. Mingzong loved him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he was tall and formidable—quiet, dutiful, and few of words—yet a terror in the field. Mingzong doted on him.

sentences.zh: 自晉兵戰梁於河上，從珂常立戰功，莊宗呼其小字曰：「阿三不徒與我同年，其敢戰亦類我。」

translations.literal: From the time Jin troops fought Liang on the Yellow River, Congke often won distinction. Zhuangzong called him by his childhood name and said: “Asan is not merely my age-mate; his boldness in battle is like mine.”
translations.idiomatic: While Jin and Liang battled along the Yellow River, Congke piled up merit. Zhuangzong used his pet name and said, “Asan is more than a comrade of my years—he fights the way I do.”

sentences.zh: 同光二年，為衛州刺史突騎指揮使，戍於石門。

translations.literal: In Tongguang 2 he became prefect of Weizhou and commander of the surprise cavalry, garrisoning Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 2 (924) he was made prefect of Weizhou and commander of the surprise cavalry, stationed at Shimen.

sentences.zh: 明宗討趙在禮，自魏反兵而南，從珂率戍兵自曲陽、孟縣馳出常山以追明宗。

translations.literal: When Mingzong campaigned against Zhao Zaili and turned his army south from Wei, Congke led garrison troops from Quyang and Meng county in a dash through Changshan to overtake Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong marched south from Wei against Zhao Zaili, Congke swept down from Quyang and Meng county through Changshan to join him.

sentences.zh: 明宗之南也，兵少，得從珂兵在後，而軍聲大振。

translations.literal: As Mingzong marched south his force was small; with Congke’s troops coming up behind, the army’s renown swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong’s column was thin on the road south, but Congke’s detachment in the rear made the host seem suddenly vast.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，拜從珂河中節度使，封潞王。

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered and took the throne, he appointed Congke military governor of Hezhong and enfeoffed him as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzong seized the throne he made Congke military governor of Hezhong and created him Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 是時，明宗春秋已高，王於諸子次最長，樞密使安重誨患之，乃矯詔河中裨將楊彥溫使圖之。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong’s years were already advanced. Among the princes the Prince of Lu stood first in seniority. An Chonghui, Bureau Military Affairs commissioner, feared him and forged an edict ordering Yang Yanwen, a deputy general in Hezhong, to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was old by then, and the Prince of Lu outranked every other son. An Chonghui, who controlled the Bureau of Military Affairs, grew alarmed and forged orders for Yang Yanwen, a Hezhong subordinate, to move against him.

sentences.zh: 王閱馬於黃龍莊，彥溫即閉門拒之，王止於虞鄉以聞。

translations.literal: The prince was reviewing horses at Yellow Dragon Manor when Yanwen shut the gates against him. The prince halted at Yuxiang and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: While the prince exercised horses at Yellow Dragon Manor, Yanwen barred the gates. He camped at Yuxiang and sent word to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明宗召王還京師，居之清化裏第。

translations.literal: Mingzong summoned the prince back to the capital and lodged him in the residence on Qinghua Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong recalled him to Luoyang and housed him in the mansion on Qinghua Lane.

sentences.zh: 重誨數請行軍法，明宗不聽，後重誨見殺，乃起王為左衛大將軍、西京留守。

translations.literal: Chonghui repeatedly asked that military law be applied; Mingzong would not listen. Later Chonghui was killed, and only then was the prince raised as grand general of the Left Guard and defender of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui pressed again and again for court-martial; Mingzong refused. After Chonghui’s fall the prince was restored as Left Guard grand general and defender of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 長興三年，為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: In Changxing 3 he became military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 3 (932) he received Fengxiang as his circuit.

sentences.zh: 王子重吉自明宗時典禁兵，為控鶴指揮使，湣帝即位，朱弘昭、馮赟用事，乃罷重吉兵職，出為亳州團練使。

translations.literal: The prince’s son Chongji had commanded the forbidden troops since Mingzong’s day as Crane Control commander. When the Min Emperor acceded, Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun held power; they removed Chongji from his military post and sent him out as training commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Congke’s son Chongji had held the inner army since Mingzong’s reign as Crane Control commander. Once Conghou took the throne, Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun stripped him of command and posted him to Bozhou as training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又徙王為北京留守，不降制書而宣授，又以李從璋為代。

translations.literal: They also transferred the prince to be defender of the Northern Capital, appointing him by oral edict without a formal rescript, and sent Li Congzhang to replace him at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: They shifted the prince to Taiyuan as metropolitan defender—by word of mouth, with no written patent—and installed Li Congzhang at Fengxiang in his place.

sentences.zh: 初，安重誨得罪罷河中，以從璋為代，而重誨見殺，故王益自疑，遂據城反。

translations.literal: Earlier, when An Chonghui fell from favor and left Hezhong, Congzhang had replaced him; when Chonghui was killed the prince grew all the more suspicious, seized the city, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhang had once succeeded An Chonghui at Hezhong when Chonghui fell. Chonghui’s execution only deepened the prince’s fears; he closed Fengxiang and rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 湣帝遣王思同會諸鎮兵討之，思同戰敗走，諸鎮兵皆潰。

translations.literal: The Min Emperor sent Wang Sitong to gather the armies of the circuits against him. Sitong was defeated and fled; the armies of the circuits all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Conghou sent Wang Sitong to rally the provincial hosts. Sitong was routed, and every allied column broke apart.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年三月丁巳，王以兵東。

translations.literal: In Qingtai 1, in the third month on dingsi, the prince marched east with his army.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi of the third month of Qingtai 1 (934) the prince drove his army east.

sentences.zh: 庚申，次長安，西京副留守劉遂雍叛於唐，來降。

translations.literal: On gengshen he halted at Chang’an. Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of the Western Capital, rebelled against Tang and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he reached Chang’an. Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of Luoyang, broke with the Tang court and submitted.

sentences.zh: 甲子，次華州，執藥彥稠。

translations.literal: On jiazi he halted at Hua prefecture and seized Yao Yanchou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he paused at Hua prefecture and took Yao Yanchou prisoner.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，次靈寶，河中安彥威、陜州康思立叛於唐，來降。

translations.literal: On bingyin he halted at Lingbao. An Yanwei of Hezhong and Kang Sil of Shan prefecture rebelled against Tang and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin he camped at Lingbao. An Yanwei in Hezhong and Kang Sil in Shanzhou turned their backs on the court and joined him.

sentences.zh: 己巳，次陜州。

translations.literal: On jisi he halted at Shan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he halted at Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 康義誠叛於唐，來降。

translations.literal: Kang Yicheng rebelled against Tang and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yicheng abandoned the Tang cause and came over.

sentences.zh: 殺宣徽使孟漢瓊。

translations.literal: Meng Hanqiong, Palace Secretariat commissioner, was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The court had Meng Hanqiong, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, put to death.

sentences.zh: 愍帝出居於衛州。

translations.literal: The Min Emperor went out to reside at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Min Emperor was sent to live at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬申，入京師，馮道率百官迎王於蔣橋，王辭不見。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renshen, he entered the capital. Feng Dao led the hundred officials to welcome the prince at Jiang Bridge; the prince declined and would not meet them.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen of the fourth month, in summer, he entered Luoyang. Feng Dao brought the bureaucracy to Jiang Bridge to welcome the prince, who refused to show himself.

sentences.zh: 入哭於西宮，遂見群臣，道拜，王答拜。

translations.literal: He entered to mourn at the Western Palace, then met the officials. Dao bowed and the prince returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to weep at the Western Palace, then received the ministers. Feng Dao bowed; the prince bowed in return.

sentences.zh: 入居於至德宮。

translations.literal: He entered to reside at Zhide Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He took up residence in Zhide Palace.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以太后令降天子為鄂王，命王監國。

translations.literal: On guiyou, by order of the empress dowager, the Son of Heaven was demoted to Prince of E and the prince was ordered to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the empress dowager’s edict demoted Conghou to Prince of E and put Congke in charge of the realm as regent.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，皇帝即位。

translations.literal: On yihai the emperor ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Deposed Emperor took the throne.

sentences.zh: 丙子，率河南民財以賞軍。

translations.literal: On bingzi he levied the wealth of the people of Henan to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi he stripped Henan households to pay off the troops.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，借民房課五月以賞軍。

translations.literal: On dingchou he borrowed private dwellings’ fifth-month tax levy to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he seized private homes and took a fifth-month rent to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，弒鄂王，義與「弒濟陰王」同。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Prince of E was murdered; the meaning is the same as “murdered the Prince of Jiyin.”
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the Prince of E was murdered; the wording has the same force as “murdered the Prince of Jiyin.”

sentences.zh: 慈州刺史宋令詢死之。

translations.literal: Song Lingxun, prefect of Cizhou, died for him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lingxun, prefect of Cizhou, died in his defense.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On yiyou a great amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the new emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 戊子，殺康義誠及藥彥稠。

translations.literal: On wuzi Kang Yicheng and Yao Yanchou were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Kang Yicheng and Yao Yanchou were put to death.

sentences.zh: 義誠叛于愍帝，罪宜曰「誅」，而廢帝同惡相殺，故書曰「殺」。

translations.literal: Yicheng rebelled against Mindi, and for his crime it should have said “executed,” but Feidi and he were partners in evil who killed one another, and therefore the text says “killed.”
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yicheng rebelled against Mindi, so his crime should have been recorded as execution. But Feidi and Yicheng were partners in evil who killed each other, so the text says “killed.”

sentences.zh: 五月丙午，端明殿學士、左諫議大夫韓昭胤為樞密使，莊宅使劉延朗為樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingwu, Han Zhaoyin, Duanming Hall academician and Left Remonstrance grand counsellor, was made Bureau Military Affairs commissioner; Liu Yanlang, manor commissioner, was made deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu of the fifth month Han Zhaoyin, academician of the Duanming Hall and Left Remonstrance counsellor, became Bureau Military Affairs commissioner, with manor commissioner Liu Yanlang as deputy.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，馮道罷。

translations.literal: On gengxu Feng Dao was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Feng Dao left office.

sentences.zh: 天雄軍節度使範延光為樞密使。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang, military governor of the Tianxiong army, was made Bureau Military Affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang, military governor of Tianxiong, was named Bureau Military Affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，賜勸進選人、宗子官。

translations.literal: On jiayin offices were bestowed on those who had submitted memorials urging enthronement and on members of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he rewarded men who had memorialized for his accession and granted posts to clansmen.

sentences.zh: 六月庚辰，幸範延光及索自通第。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengchen, he visited the mansions of Fan Yanguang and Suo Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen of the sixth month he called at the homes of Fan Yanguang and Suo Zitong.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛亥，太常卿盧文紀為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinhai, Lu Wenji, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly with the Secretariat Under the Gate Pallarak Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai of the seventh month, in autumn, Lu Wenji, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, entered the Secretariat as vice director and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，立沛國夫人劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On dingsi the Lady Liu of Pei State was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Lady Liu of Pei was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 八月辛未，尚書左丞姚顗為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinwei, Yao Ting, Left Vice Director of the Ministries, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly with the Secretariat Under the Gate Pallarak Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei of the eighth month Yao Ting, left vice director of the ministries, joined the Secretariat as vice director and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 許御署官選。

translations.literal: The selection of yushu officials was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court permitted the selection of yushu officials.

sentences.zh: 「御署官」，疑是廢帝初舉兵時所置之官，以其非吏部正授，故須有旨方得選。

translations.literal: “Yushu officials” were probably officials established when Feidi first raised troops; because they were not regular appointments by the Ministry of Personnel, an imperial order was required before they could be selected.
translations.idiomatic: The “yushu officials” were probably offices created when Feidi first raised troops. Since they were not regular Ministry of Personnel appointments, they required an imperial order before they could be selected.

sentences.zh: 此於事無勸戒，不必書，以舊史不詳，故存所不知，慎傳疑也。

translations.literal: This has no encouragement or warning in the matter and need not have been written; because the old history is unclear, it preserves what is not known, cautiously transmitting doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The matter carries no lesson of praise or warning and did not need to be recorded; because the old history is unclear, the text preserves the uncertainty and carefully transmits the doubt.

sentences.zh: 九月，契丹寇邊。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Khitan raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Khitan forces struck the frontier.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊寅，李愚、劉句罷。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, Li Yu and Liu Gou were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin of the tenth month, in winter, Li Yu and Liu Gou left office.

sentences.zh: 十二月己亥，雄武軍節度使張延郎為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jihai, Zhang Yanlang, military governor of the Xiongwu army, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly with the Secretariat Under the Gate Pallarak Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai of the twelfth month Zhang Yanlang of Xiongwu became vice director of the Secretariat and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇雲州。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Yun prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan raiders struck Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，幸龍門。

translations.literal: On gengyin he visited Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he traveled to Longmen.

sentences.zh: 旱。

translations.literal: There was drought.
translations.idiomatic: Drought gripped the land.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月甲戌，範延光罷。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, the second month, on jiaxu, Fan Yanguang was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu of the second month in the spring of his second year, Fan Yanguang left office.

sentences.zh: 己丑，追尊魯國太夫人魏氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On jichou the Grand Lady Wei of Lu State was posthumously honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the court posthumously raised Congke’s mother, Grand Lady Wei of Lu, to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 非嫡母，故詳其爵氏。

translations.literal: She was not the legitimate mother, and therefore her title and clan are detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Because she was not the legitimate mother, the text gives her title and clan in detail.

sentences.zh: 三月辛丑，忠武軍節度使趙延壽為樞密使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinchou, Zhao Yanshou, military governor of the Zhongwu army, was made Bureau Military Affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou of the third month Zhao Yanshou, military governor of Zhongwu, became Bureau Military Affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 夏五月辛卯，宣徽南院使劉延皓為樞密使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on xinmao, Liu Yanhao, commissioner of the southern Palace Secretariat bureau, was made Bureau Military Affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao of the fifth month, in summer, Liu Yanhao of the southern Palace Secretariat bureau took the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇邊。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan forces again raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未，群臣獻添都馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guiwei, the officials presented additional capital horses.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei of the sixth month the ministers offered extra horses for the capital guard.

sentences.zh: 「都」者，軍伍之名。

translations.literal: “Du” is the name of a military unit.
translations.idiomatic: “Du” was the name of a military unit.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁酉，回鶻可汗王仁美使其都督陳福海來。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingyou, the Uyghur khan Wang Renmei sent his commissioner Chen Fuhai.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou of the seventh month, in autumn, Wang Renmei of the Uyghurs sent his commissioner Chen Fuhai.

sentences.zh: 劉延皓罷。

translations.literal: Liu Yanhao was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanhao left office.

sentences.zh: 九月己酉，刑部尚書房暠為樞密使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiyou, Fang Gao, director of the Ministry of Punishments, was made Bureau Military Affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou of the ninth month Fang Gao, minister of punishments, became Bureau Military Affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，渤海遣使者來。

translations.literal: On yimao Bohai sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao envoys arrived from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月乙未，百濟遣使者來。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, the first month, on yiwei, Baekje sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei of the first month in the spring of his third year, envoys came from Baekje.

sentences.zh: 丁未，封子重美為雍王。

translations.literal: On dingwei his son Chongmei was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei his son Chongmei was created Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 三月丙午，翰林學士、禮部侍郎馬胤孫為中書侍郎，同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingwu, Ma Yinsun, Hanlin academician and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly with the Secretariat Under the Gate Pallarak Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu of the third month Ma Yinsun, Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites, joined the Secretariat as vice director and grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使石敬瑭反。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang, military governor of Hedong, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang, military governor of Hedong, rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 夏五月乙卯，建雄軍節度使張敬達為太原四面都招討使，義武軍節度使楊光遠為副。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yimao, Zhang Jingda, military governor of the Jianxiong army, was made grand suppression commissioner on all four sides of Taiyuan; Yang Guangyuan, military governor of the Yiwu army, was made deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao of the fifth month, in summer, Zhang Jingda of Jianxiong became grand suppression commissioner for Taiyuan on every side, with Yang Guangyuan of Yiwu as his second.

sentences.zh: 戊申，先鋒指揮使安審信叛降於石敬瑭。

translations.literal: On wushen An Shenxin, vanguard commander, rebelled and surrendered to Shi Jingtang.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the vanguard commander An Shenxin defected to Shi Jingtang.

sentences.zh: 己酉，振武戍將安重榮叛降於石敬瑭。

translations.literal: On jiyou An Chongrong, garrison officer of Zhenwu, rebelled and surrendered to Shi Jingtang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou An Chongrong, officer of the Zhenwu garrison, went over to Shi Jingtang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，天雄軍屯駐捧聖都虞候張令昭逐其節度使劉延皓。

translations.literal: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao, deputy commander of the Bearer-of-Sagacity command in the Tianxiong army garrison, expelled his military governor Liu Yanhao.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao, deputy of the Bearer-of-Sagacity command at the Tianxiong encampment, drove out his military governor Liu Yanhao.

sentences.zh: 六月癸亥，以令昭為右千牛衛將軍，權知天雄軍事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guihai, Lingzhao was made general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and given acting authority over Tianxiong military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai of the sixth month Lingzhao was made a general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and left in temporary charge of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 佗命官不書「以」，此書「以」者，明令昭猶可「以」。

translations.literal: Other appointments do not write “by appointing”; this writes “by appointing” to make clear that Lingzhao could still be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Other appointments do not use the word “by.” It is used here to show that Lingzhao could still be appointed.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，宣武軍節度使範延光為天雄軍四面招討使。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Fan Yanguang, military governor of the Xuanwu army, was made suppression commissioner on all four sides of the Tianxiong army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Fan Yanguang of Xuanwu became suppression commissioner for Tianxiong on every side.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊申，克魏州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wushen, Weizhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen of the seventh month, in autumn, the imperial army captured Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，張令昭伏誅。

translations.literal: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao was put to death.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，彰聖指揮使張萬迪叛降於石敬瑭。

translations.literal: On guichou Zhang Wandi, commander of the Zhangsheng guard, rebelled and surrendered to Shi Jingtang.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Zhang Wandi of the Zhangsheng command went over to Shi Jingtang.

sentences.zh: 八月戊午，契丹使梅裏來。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuwu, the Khitan envoy Meili came.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu of the eighth month the Khitan envoy Meili arrived.

sentences.zh: 九月甲辰，張敬達及契丹戰於太原，敗績，契丹圍敬達於晉安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiachen, Zhang Jingda and the Khitan fought at Taiyuan and suffered a great defeat; the Khitan surrounded Jingda at Jin’an.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen of the ninth month Zhang Jingda met the Khitan at Taiyuan and was shattered; they penned him in at Jin’an.

sentences.zh: 戊申，如河陽。

translations.literal: On wushen he went to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Deposed Emperor moved to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬戌，括馬，籍民為兵。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, horses were conscripted and the people were registered as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu of the tenth month, in winter, the court seized horses and enrolled commoners as troops.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊子，盧龍軍節度使趙德鈞為行營都統。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuzi, Zhao Dejun, military governor of the Lulong army, was made commander-in-chief of the campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi of the eleventh month Zhao Dejun of Lulong became commander-in-chief of the field army.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，契丹立晉。

translations.literal: On dingyou the Khitan established Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the Khitan enthroned the Later Jin.

sentences.zh: 閏月甲子，楊光遠殺張敬達，以其軍叛降於契丹。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on jiazi, Yang Guangyuan killed Zhang Jingda, led his army in defection, and surrendered to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the intercalary month Yang Guangyuan murdered Zhang Jingda and took his army over to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 敬達不書死之而書「殺」者，敬達大將，宜以義責光遠而誅之，雖不果而見殺，猶為得死，乃諷光遠殺己以叛，故書之如其志。

translations.literal: That Jingda is not written as dying for it but as “killed” is because Jingda was a great general and should have rebuked Guangyuan with righteousness and executed him; even if he failed and was killed, he would still have obtained a proper death, but instead he urged Guangyuan to kill him and rebel, so the text writes it according to his intention.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda is not said to have died for the cause but to have been “killed.” As a senior general, he should have rebuked Yang Guangyuan on grounds of duty and executed him; even if he had failed and been killed, that would still have been an honorable death. Instead he urged Guangyuan to kill him and rebel, so the text records the death according to his own intention.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，契丹及晉人至於潞州。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the Khitan and the men of Jin reached Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Khitan and Jin forces arrived at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，至自河陽。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou he returned from Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day he returned from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，皇帝崩。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 年五十一，帝自焚死，晉高祖命葬其燼骨於徽陵域中。

translations.literal: He was fifty-one years old; the emperor burned himself to death, and Gaozu of Jin ordered his charred bones buried within the precinct of Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-one. The emperor burned himself to death, and Gaozu of Jin ordered his charred bones buried within the Huiling precinct.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，君臣之際，可謂難哉！

translations.literal: Alas, the juncture between ruler and minister—how difficult it is!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the bond between ruler and minister is a hard thing to sustain!

sentences.zh: 蓋明者慮於未萌而前知，暗者告以將及而不懼，故先事而言，則雖忠而不信，事至而悔，其可及乎？

translations.literal: For the clear-sighted take thought before trouble sprouts and know it beforehand; the dim are told disaster is near yet do not fear. Thus to speak before the event may be loyal yet unbelieved; when the matter arrives and one repents, can it still be reached?
translations.idiomatic: The clear-sighted foresee trouble before it sprouts; the blind are warned that disaster is near yet feel no fear. Speak too soon and loyalty may go unbelieved; wait until ruin is upon you and regret cannot catch up.

sentences.zh: 重誨區區獨見潞王之禍，而謀之不臧，至於殞身赤族，其隙自茲。

translations.literal: Chonghui alone, in his narrow way, saw the calamity of the Prince of Lu, yet his plotting was ill-conceived, until he perished and his clan was extinguished—the rift began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui alone, in his narrow wisdom, foresaw the Prince of Lu's doom, yet schemed badly and ended with his own death and his clan wiped out—the breach began here.

sentences.zh: 及湣帝之亡也，穴於徽陵，其土一壟，路人見者，皆為之悲。

translations.literal: When the Min Emperor perished he was buried in a pit at Huiling; a single mound of earth—and passersby who saw it all grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Min Emperor died he was laid in a shallow grave at Huiling, a single mound of earth; travelers who passed by all mourned for him.

sentences.zh: 使明宗為有知，其有愧於重誨矣，哀哉！

translations.literal: Had Mingzong consciousness in the grave, he would feel shame toward Chonghui—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: If Mingzong could know from beyond the grave, he would blush for Chonghui—how lamentable!
